areas.name: PlayStation 3 Route and Controls
areas.location_cue: The PlayStation 3 title menu and the first aiming gallery.
areas.note: Configure the selected platform route before permanent progress begins.

levels.1: The chosen route adds high-definition presentation and two aiming options.
levels.2: Play the 2012 PlayStation 3 release rather than the original Wii edition.
levels.3: Use the PlayStation 3 version, create a fresh system save, and keep separate chapter-progress and rank-cleanup saves; the Wii release adds no exclusive completion content for this route.

levels.1: A steady reticle matters more than rapid camera movement.
levels.2: Test reticle speed and dead zone with a DualShock controller before saving progress.
levels.3: Enter the first playable gallery, lower aim speed until small props can be tracked without overshoot, confirm both sticks recenter cleanly, then preserve those settings for every rank attempt.

levels.1: The pointer route needs an unobstructed sensor view.
levels.2: Recenter the Move pointer at the television edges before the first chapter.
levels.3: Seat the camera securely, calibrate from the actual playing position, trace all four screen edges, and verify the cursor neither drifts nor clips before relying on it for brief file targets.

levels.1: Several different actions contribute to each results grade.
levels.2: Track clear time, enemy hits, critical hits, destroyed objects, and collected files.
levels.3: At each results screen compare all five categories. Replays retain previously found files, so obtain collectibles first, then optimize speed, accuracy, critical hits, and destructible-object totals on later rank runs.

levels.1: Higher chapter grades fund armory progress faster.
levels.2: A results grade pays four stars for S, three for A, two for B, or one for C.
levels.3: Record every award before buying upgrades. Replay a short comfortable chapter for more stars whenever the remaining armory cost exceeds the current balance; star income is repeatable.
